clue.text: Most original of three points?

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass
E, east, is a second compass point
west is the third compass point

explanation.surface: A question about which of three dots on a page came first.
explanation.walkthrough: The three compass points are spelt two ways: two as single letters, N and E, and the third written out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most original is the freshest and most recent, a superlative synonym.

clue.text: Little boy turns up with drink — it could go either girl in part of France

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Little boy turns up with drink — it could go either girl in part of France', is garbled (text from 22-down mixed in); the likely parse is rev(RON) + MANDY but 'with drink' and 'it could go either' fit nothing
annotationWithheld.clue: Little boy turns up with drink — it could go either girl in part of France

clue.text: Switch attack, given injury

parts.note: a switch is a thin flexible cane, a whip
to lash is to attack with blows or words

explanation.surface: Someone changes their method of assault and gets hurt in the process.
explanation.definitionFit: A neck injury caused by a sudden jerk, typically in a car collision.

clue.text: Leave out rubbish con

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Leave out rubbish con', looks cut short (probably 'container'): 'con' gives nothing toward SKIP, and the OCR fix is beyond three letters

clue.text: Importance of same ship at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters before it are mixed up

explanation.surface: Comparing how much a sister ship matters while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' turns the letters of SAME SHIP into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress or weight placed on something, its significance.

clue.text: Female constantly evolving in more than unusual Italian city, not in English

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of more than come in an odd order
not removes the next word's letters from the city

parts.note: Turin is a city in northern Italy

explanation.surface: A woman keeps developing in a strange Italian city, but not in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' is the anagram signal for MORE THAN, and 'not in' removes those two letters from the city; the definition personifies nature as a woman always changing.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified creative force of the natural world, pictured as a woman, keeps changing through evolution.

clue.text: Don't sing with piano, for A A A the blues

parts.note: to hum is to make a tune without singing the words
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Humming along to the piano as a cure for feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hump' is British slang for a fit of sulkiness or gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a person with the hump is sulky or depressed, a low mood.

clue.text: Bottle of brandy, for instance

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve
brandy is one example of a distilled strong drink

explanation.surface: A bottle containing brandy, offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means courage, the same as British 'bottle', and also any distilled liquor such as brandy.

clue.text: Put off woman, having to exist without one

parts.note: she is the pronoun used for a woman

indicators.note: without signals that the letter for one is dropped from the verb

parts.note: to live is to exist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman is discouraged because she has to survive alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the Roman one from the verb; 'Put off' looks like discouraging a woman but means postpone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to postpone it, setting it aside for later.

clue.text: It's dried up, so sun god has answered the door?

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
someone who answers the door is at home, that is, is in

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the sun god opening his front door, with something shrivelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's dried up' is the definition: a grape that has been dried.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape, the fruit that has lost its moisture in the sun.

clue.text: Some characters taken from camp to main exit in smelly compound

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the following words are used, a run lifted out of them

explanation.surface: A few people leave the camp by the main exit near a foul-smelling chemical works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines are foul-smelling nitrogen compounds produced when protein decays.

clue.text: A pantomime so ridiculous would be from SW Asia

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters of the phrase are made absurdly jumbled

explanation.surface: A silly pantomime could only have come from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges A PANTOMIME SO; 'would be' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesopotamia was the ancient land between the Tigris and Euphrates, in modern Iraq, south-west Asia.

clue.text: Shaft appears very big in hospital department

indicators.note: in places the size letters inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: A and E is the British accident and emergency department
XL is the clothing size extra large

explanation.surface: A very large shaft turns up in the emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or spindle on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Floor has to come clean

definitions.meaning: a floor of a building, one storey

explanation.surface: A floor needs to be cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: A level is a storey of a building, and to level with someone is to confess honestly.

clue.text: Capital, or capitals of Kenya, Iceland, Egypt and Venezuela

indicators.note: capitals here means the initial capital letters of each country named

explanation.surface: Naming a capital city, or the capitals of four countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for capital cities; the wordplay wants capital letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now usually spelt Kyiv, is the capital city of Ukraine.

clue.text: Rabbit on jet

definitions.meaning: to rabbit on is British slang for talking at length
a jet is a stream of liquid forced out

explanation.surface: A rabbit riding a jet plane.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to talk on and on, and a spout is a gushing stream of water.

clue.text: Show, but not a party

indicators.note: but not tells us the letter after it is removed from the verb

parts.note: to reveal is to show

explanation.surface: It's a show, but not a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a' drops A from REVEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively celebration, a noisy festivity.

clue.text: Sad, having been sacked?

explanation.surface: Is someone unhappy because they lost their job?
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed means let down and unhappy; split as dis-appointed it jokingly means removed from a post.

clue.text: Actress eating lots of eale

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Actress eating lots of eale', is garbled: 'eale' is no word and the corrected word (perhaps 'cash' for RICH) cannot be confirmed

clue.text: Acrobatic feat on foot?

definitions.meaning: something worn on the foot, a rubber sandal

explanation.surface: A gymnastic move performed on one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flop is a gymnast's backflip and also a thong sandal held on by a toe strap.

clue.text: Plain paper manufacturer's managerial job description?

definitions.meaning: the manager of a paper mill would run it, read literally

explanation.surface: Asking what a paper mill's manager does all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Run-of-the-mill means ordinary; read literally it describes running a mill.

clue.text: Country where bears will roam around one

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters on either side of the numeral
roaming wanders about, so the letters of bears move around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A country where bears wander freely around a single spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will roam' rearranges BEARS into SERBA, and 'around' wraps it about I.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a landlocked Balkan state with Belgrade as its capital.

clue.text: Drunkard overturning drink — it could go either way

indicators.note: overturning means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drunk knocks his glass over, and the outcome is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' flips the drunkard word round; the drink at the end is the verb sup, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is an even chance, like a coin flip whose result is uncertain.

clue.text: God has delicate back

indicators.note: back means the word is to be read from end to start

parts.note: sore and delicate both describe tender skin

explanation.surface: A god with a sensitive back.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Dangerous state of armpit?

definitions.meaning: an underarm is usually covered in hair

explanation.surface: Asking whether an underarm is a hazardous condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is informal for risky and frightening, and literally describes a hair-covered underarm.

clue.text: Block vessels in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse says the word is read backwards

parts.note: pots are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: Ships are stopped by reversing into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse' turns POTS round; 'vessels' suggests ships but means pots.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to block or plug it.

clue.text: Smear with endless advertising text

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Smear with endless advertising text', gives no S: BLURB less its ends gives LUR, and 'with' supplies nothing; likely an OCR misreading that cannot be confirmed

clue.text: Transport initially taken aside

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: split as a side: a plus a sports team of eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Transport is first taken to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'aside' into 'a side': a team of eleven players, written XI as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a means of getting around.

clue.text: Taken from a rock when in the sea

indicators.note: in puts the word for when inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is the sea of northern Europe
as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: Something comes from a rock while out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Basaltic means made of or derived from basalt, a dark volcanic stone.

clue.text: Boy having trouble with a den? Lion not on!

indicators.note: having trouble suggests the following letters are disordered and in difficulty
not removes the letters of the following word from the animal

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A lad is in trouble in a den, but the lion is not on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on' removes ON from LION, leaving LI; 'having trouble' mixes A DEN and LI. The biblical Daniel survived the lions' den.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a boy's name, borne by the prophet thrown to the lions.

clue.text: It's clear, father's turned on himself?

indicators.note: turned means the short word is flipped round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for a father
the father himself is a parent

explanation.surface: It's obvious that the father has turned against himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes PA into AP, and 'himself', the father again, gives PARENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or evident.

clue.text: Man taking encore at dance

parts.note: bis is a call for a repeat performance, an encore
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A man performs an encore at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess each piece is a man, and the bishop is one of them.
